political-political-5/beat-08.text: Locke and Rousseau ask what makes them legitimate. Mill asks how far they may bind you.

political-political-5/beat-09.text: Plato and Rawls ask what justice demands.

political-political-6/beat-00.text: Would you accept this society if you turned out to be the poorest in it? Rawls turned that question into a test for justice itself.

political-political-6/beat-01.text: Back behind the veil of ignorance, you choose the rules not knowing who you’ll be. Rawls says two principles fall out of that fair start, in strict order.

political-political-6/beat-02.text: First: each person gets the same basic liberties, and these come first. Second: inequalities are allowed only if they help the least advantaged and attach to jobs open to all.

political-political-6/beat-04.text: Is a surgeon earning far more than a clerk unjust? Not necessarily.

political-political-6/beat-05.text: The gap is just when higher pay draws talent that lifts even the worst-off above the equality line. The test is the bottom, not the top.

political-political-7/beat-00.text: You’re allowed to say what you think. So who handed you that?

political-political-7/beat-01.text: A government? A piece of paper?

political-political-7/beat-02.text: Or was it yours before anyone voted on anything?

political-political-7/beat-03.text: John Locke pointed at the ground. Some things are yours the moment you exist — your life, your freedom, your stuff.

political-political-7/beat-04.text: Nobody grants your rights. A government exists to guard them, not to hand them out.

political-political-7/beat-05.text: Others pointed up here instead. A right is something people wrote down, signed, and agreed to enforce.

political-political-7/beat-06.text: No signature, no right — just a wish said loudly.

political-political-7/beat-08.text: Here’s how to tell the two apart. Tomorrow a government passes a law: from now on, you may not say what you think.

political-political-7/beat-09.text: The law is real, and it’s enforced.

political-political-7/beat-11.text: Watch what the law can reach. It tears the paper in half, and the stone does not move.

political-political-7/beat-12.text: That’s the claim: rights you have just for being human. A government can break one.

political-political-7/beat-15.text: And the claim has teeth. Thinkers announced the rights of man, then quietly stopped at men.

political-political-7/beat-16.text: Mary Wollstonecraft pressed the logic: if rights come from being a reasoning human, women are that too.

political-political-8/beat-01.text: A match on the far side that all three want to watch. Everybody agrees they should get to.

political-political-8/beat-02.text: Now watch how fast agreeing falls apart.

political-political-8/beat-03.text: Nobody here cheated anybody. They were born different heights.

political-political-8/beat-04.text: The tall one sees the whole pitch. The short one sees a plank of wood.

political-political-8/beat-05.text: Luckily somebody left three crates by the gate. Three crates, three people.

political-political-8/beat-06.text: You can’t get fairer than one each. Can you?

political-political-8/beat-07.text: One crate each. Same size, same share, nobody favoured, nobody skipped.

political-political-8/beat-08.text: And the shortest one is still looking at wood.

political-political-8/beat-10.text: Nothing was added and nothing was thrown away. The same three crates, moved to where they actually do something.

political-political-8/beat-11.text: Look at the eye line now — dead level.

political-political-8/beat-13.text: So equality is a blank waiting to be filled in. Equal resources?

political-political-8/beat-15.text: Amartya Sen and Martha Nussbaum answer differently. Make capabilities equal: what a person can really do and be.

political-political-9/beat-00.text: Rule by the people. Four of them here, and one over there who wants something the four do not.

political-political-9/beat-01.text: So they vote, and the count is honest, and the count is seven to one. Plato distrusted this: steering a ship takes a trained pilot, not a show of hands.

political-political-9/beat-02.text: Let the crew vote and they follow whoever flatters them best.

political-political-9/beat-03.text: Nothing has gone wrong with the procedure. Everyone got a vote, the larger number won, and now the larger number is walking toward the smaller one.

political-political-9/beat-04.text: This is democracy working, not democracy failing.

political-political-9/beat-06.text: Mill and Tocqueville both named the danger, and both drew a line no vote can cross. That’s why a court can strike down a law the majority voted for.
